segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Nagel Line is the tritangent counterpart of the Euler line, passing through the Incenter X one, the Centroid X two, the Nagel Point X eight, and the Spieker Center X ten.

segments.text: Because the Spieker Center X ten is the incenter of the medial triangle, and the medial triangle is the image of triangle A B C under homothety at X two with factor negative one-half, X ten is the complement of X one, and the Nagel Point X eight is the anticomplement of X one.

segments.text: Just as Xthree, X two, X five, and X four divide the Euler line in the ratio two to one to three, X one, X two, X ten, and X eight divide the Nagel line in the exact same proportion: two to one to three.
